bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds fully allocated to capex for manufacturing expansion; acquisition of 88% stake in Gravus Tech for GTM expansion; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on reinvestment into R&D and new verticals
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: U.S. market delays due to geopolitical tensions and tariffs; supply chain disruptions from Middle East instability; margin pressure from raw material inflation; execution risk in scaling new verticals (Hearables, EMS, Energy); customer concentration risk in legacy Home Lighting (Signify) despite diversification
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and forward-looking; management emphasizes ODM solutioning over product selling, highlights operational flexibility, and frames challenges (geopolitics, margins) as temporary; tone is bullish on long-term diversification and global positioning
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Hearables/Wearables segment is being moved from subsidiary to parent company to streamline ops — signals strategic prioritization; company is not competing with Lumax/FIEM but supplying LED sources to their products — Tier 2 supplier with high-value design IP; 80-85% of business is ODM, not OEM, indicating strong design IP and customer lock-in; solar + battery offering is bundled with EMS, creating end-to-end energy solutions
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds are the named funding source for the greenfield capacity expansion.
- Balance sheet is equity-heavy and lightly levered: total equity Rs 6,094 Mn at Mar-26 (vs Rs 5,620 Mn at Mar-25) against non-current borrowings of Rs 13 Mn and current borrowings of Rs 399 Mn.
- Reinvestment is visible in working capital and capex: inventories rose to Rs 2,011 Mn (from Rs 1,388 Mn) and capital WIP to Rs 956 Mn (from Rs 437 Mn), while cash and bank fell to Rs 576 Mn (from Rs 1,097 Mn) over Mar-25 to Mar-26.
- The deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or a stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Lighting: 23% of Q4 revenue (down from prior years), ODM Home Lighting still with Signify but diversifying to other top 5 Indian brands; Commercial/Refrigeration: leading supplier; Automotive: new aftermarket LED source supplier to multinational brands (NDAs in place); Hearables/Wearables: 60% OEM, transitioning to ODM, margins in high single digits targeting double digits; Energy: solar inverters + batteries launched; EMS: new vertical in Tower 1, supplying Honeywell for PA systems and sensors
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Describes itself as "a leading ODM (Original Design Manufacturer) specializing in the design, development and manufacturing of energy-efficient lighting and electronic solutions for global markets", backed by in-house R&D and backward-integrated capabilities serving "marquee clients".
- Stated vision: "To be a preferred manufacturing and solutions provider of Lighting, Energy Efficient Products, Electronic Components and Hardware Components in the global marketplace."
- Claims ~25 years of relevant experience, 3,000+ SKUs developed in-house, and an in-house R&D and product design team of ~50+ employees.
- Globalisation strategy: "Expanded global footprint to 20+ countries"; revenue from outside India grew 53% YoY to Rs 1,101 Mn with contribution rising to 18% in FY26 (vs 15% in FY25); FY26 mix shown as 82% India / 18% Outside India.
- Company was renamed from IKIO Lighting Limited to IKIO Technologies Limited; listed on BSE and NSE w.e.f. June 16, 2023.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Name change] Now IKIO Technologies Limited, "Formerly known as IKIO Lighting Limited" (CIN L31401DL2016PLC292884), reflecting the shift beyond lighting.
- [Customer anchors] Deck names Philips India (Signify) as the customer for whom a dedicated LED supply facility was set up, and Honeywell India as the customer for wiring devices.
- [Board] Chairman & MD Hardeep Singh; Sanjeet Singh holds the combined Whole Time Director, CEO and CFO roles; four independent directors including a former CMD of Steel Authority of India and a former MD & CEO of Vijaya Bank.
- [Policy tailwinds cited] China+1 supply-chain diversification and PLI-led localisation are named as the structural drivers enabling entry into higher-value EMS, alongside a stated sector shift from Low-Mix High-Volume to High-Mix Low-Volume manufacturing.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expansion from 13% (FY26) to 15-16% (FY27 guidance) driven by operating leverage as new verticals scale; current margins depressed by front-loaded R&D, capex, and 2,500+ headcount; raw material cost inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by design flexibility and customer price adjustments
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 20-22% YoY in FY27; margin: 15-16% EBITDA; order inflow: expected to grow with new customers in Automotive, Honeywell EMS, and Middle East lighting; capex/commissioning: Block II of 2 lakh sq.ft greenfield facility to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27, total capex funded via IPO proceeds
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No formal order book; revenue driven by ODM planning with customer volume forecasts and pipeline, not contractual backlog
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into U.S. solar and electronics market (ready plan, delayed by geopolitics); entry into premium European residential lighting; scaling Honeywell EMS contracts; leveraging 5 factories for fungible production across verticals; potential for further M&A in distribution or component tech
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: IKIO has successfully diversified from a lighting-only ODM to a multi-segment integrated technology player, with non-lighting revenue now at 77% of Q4 FY26 sales and global exports rising 53% YoY; the scaling of new verticals (Hearables, Automotive, Energy) and greenfield capacity is driving margin expansion despite front-loaded costs, positioning the company for sustained 20-22% revenue growth and 15-16% EBITDA margins in FY27.

open.item: Block II (~2 lakh sq. ft.) of the Noida Greenfield Facility is expected to be commercialised by Q1 FY27, aimed at enhancing export business and new domestic product development.
Management stated it will remain focused on accelerating clean technology and automotive electronics initiatives in FY 2026-27.
Construction of Block III (~1 lakh sq. ft.) at the Noida greenfield facility is progressing as planned, with no specific completion date disclosed.

Once all Noida greenfield blocks are fully operational, total manufacturing capacity is expected to reach 8 lakh sq. ft., strengthening export capability and supporting new domestic products (LED home lighting, solar panel systems).
Company is placing greater emphasis on soundbars, headphones and TWS earbuds within its hearables/wearables portfolio going forward, given healthy Indian audio demand.
Block III (~1 lakh sq. ft.) of the Noida Greenfield Project is currently under development with a focus on specialised and high-value product categories; no completion date disclosed.
Company is actively securing approvals for expansion into the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
Block III (~1 lakh sq. ft.) of the Noida Greenfield Facility is under construction, focused on specialised and high-value product categories, with no disclosed completion date.

Once all Noida greenfield blocks are operational, total capacity across facilities is expected to reach 8 lakh sq. ft., strengthening export capability and supporting new domestic products including LED home lighting and solar panel systems.

risks.note: The CFO role changed twice within the reporting window - Mr. Subhash Chand Agrawal (till June 30, 2024), then Mr. Atul Kumar Jain (till July 1, 2025), before Mr. Sanjeet Singh was appointed CFO in August 2025; the Deputy CFO, Mr. Naveen Bhatia, has also tendered resignation effective June 30, 2026, indicating repeated churn in the finance leadership function.

Mr. Sanjeet Singh simultaneously holds the positions of Whole-Time Director, Chief Financial Officer and Group Chief Executive Officer, concentrating operational, financial and executive authority in a single officer rather than separating these functions.
risks.risk: Concentration of executive roles in one individual

risks.note: The Board created and filled a new Chief Information Security Officer position (Mr. Narendra Prasad, appointed May 2, 2026) on the recommendation of the Risk Management Committee, and the Committee's charter explicitly names information and cyber security risk as a category it must identify and mitigate.

Mrs. Rachana Chowdhary, the Company's sole Non-Executive Woman Independent Director, resigned effective April 4, 2026; her replacement (Ms. Madhu Pandit) was appointed only as an Additional Director pending shareholder approval, leaving a temporary gap in the mandated women-independent-director composition.

The Risk Management Committee's terms of reference formally cover financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability/ESG-related, information and cyber security risk, and any other risk the Committee determines material - signalling multi-dimensional risk exposure typical of a fast-diversifying, multi-subsidiary electronics manufacturer, though the specific risk register itself is not detailed in this section.
